title: Come Work With Us—As Our New AI Associate Editor!
gist: A Lawfare job posting that doubles as disclosure of the scope and resourcing of its new AI Research Program: six named research domains spanning governance, national security, economics, the legal system, democratic institutions and catastrophic risk, delivered through analysis, podcasts, litigation trackers, commissioned papers and visiting fellows. The entry-level role pays $48,800-$60,000 remote, indicating the program is staffed thinly at the junior level.

insights.claim: Lawfare has stood up a new AI Research Program organized around six research domains: AI governance and regulation; AI and national security; AI and the economy; AI and the legal system; AI and democratic institutions; and AI safety and catastrophic risk.
insights.speaker: Tyler McBrien
insights.so_what: Maps the taxonomy an influential national-security law outlet will use to frame AI policy debate--a preview of where regulatory attention concentrates.
insights.quote: AI governance and regulation; AI and national security; AI and the economy; AI and the legal system; AI and democratic institutions; and AI safety and catastrophic risk

insights.claim: The program's output mix spans written analysis, podcasts, trackers, commissioned papers, visiting fellows, workshops and briefings, indicating an institution building durable research infrastructure rather than episodic commentary on AI.
insights.speaker: Tyler McBrien
insights.so_what: Signals that AI law and policy has become a permanent beat with dedicated funding, not a news cycle.
insights.locator: The associate editor supports the program’s written analysis

insights.claim: Lawfare maintains named AI-related tracking resources including 'AI on the Docket' and a Section 230 Tracker, plus the Scaling Laws podcast, giving outside observers structured monitoring of AI litigation and platform-liability developments.
insights.speaker: Tyler McBrien
insights.so_what: Free, structured trackers for AI litigation and Section 230 developments are a low-cost monitoring feed for platform and AI-liability exposure.

insights.claim: The role is compensated at $48,800-$60,000 per year, remote within the United States, with fully paid health and dental premiums, flexible hours and a 401(k) with up to 4% employer match.
insights.speaker: Tyler McBrien
insights.so_what: Benchmarks nonprofit AI-policy pay against private-sector AI roles--a several-fold gap that constrains think-tank talent retention.
insights.quote: Salary is competitive and commensurate with experience within a range of $48,800 - $60,000.

insights.claim: The position is explicitly entry-level and suited to recent college graduates or those with a year or two of experience, yet requires the ability to review AI-related submissions for substantive accuracy and to engage credibly with AI capabilities and their legal implications.
insights.speaker: Tyler McBrien
insights.so_what: The gap between required AI-technical judgment and entry-level pay illustrates the thinness of the AI-policy talent pipeline.

insights.claim: The job description bundles substantive editorial review with website management, publication scheduling, fundraising and donor documentation, intern hiring and general administration--evidence the AI program runs on very lean staffing.
insights.speaker: Tyler McBrien
insights.so_what: Institutional capacity in AI policy analysis is far smaller than the volume of debate suggests; influence is concentrated in a few thinly staffed shops.
